title: Implement savings estimation v1 (batching + caching) using token metering baselines
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Internal: Adds savings_estimate_v1 computation for batching/caching suggestions based on metering baselines; introduces versioned payload contract and unit tests.
body:
Context: This PR implements the first productionized savings estimation path for Optimize Suggestions (batching + caching) using recent token metering baselines. The output is a versioned, UI-consumable payload intended for the Console Suggestions (read-only beta). This work is the core deliverable for ENG-2403 (baseline cost metrics + freshness) and unblocks end-to-end rendering of “estimated savings” with a traceable basis.

What’s included: (1) Baseline aggregation job for cost/latency/token metrics keyed by (tenant_id, workspace_id, route_id, model_id, region) over a configurable lookback window; (2) Savings estimator v1 that produces projected $/1M tokens and monthly impact for two recommendation types: enable/adjust continuous batching and enable/adjust prefix/KV caching; (3) A versioned contract for the Console/optimize-suggestions-service boundary, including confidence intervals and “basis of estimate”; (4) Unit tests for estimator math, edge cases, and regression tests for double-count prevention between batching and caching recommendations when both are present for the same scope.

Estimator approach (v1): We compute a baseline_cost_per_1m_tokens from metering (gpu_ms, tokens_in/out, billed_token_units) using recent traffic, then apply a modeled multiplier for the recommended change. For batching suggestions we estimate throughput gain from target_batch_size and observed concurrency distribution (p50/p95 inflight), then convert to cost reduction via gpu_ms/token improvements. For caching suggestions we estimate expected cache hit rate from observed prefix repetition and request length distribution; savings are modeled as reduced prefill compute (gpu_ms) and reduced token processing for repeated prefixes. Monthly impact is derived from baseline token volume over the same window and is presented as an estimate (not guaranteed).

Confidence intervals and caveats: v1 exposes a simple uncertainty model via (low, mid, high) bounds around cost_per_1m_tokens and monthly_usd, driven by traffic variance, baseline window size, and missingness in metering fields. Confidence is not a separate UI primitive in this PR; instead we expose: confidence_score (0–1), ci_90_low/ci_90_high, and basis fields so Console can decide how to disclose. We explicitly clamp outputs when metering is insufficient and return a structured reason to support the “insufficient telemetry” UI state.

Data contract: Adds savings_estimate payload schema under optimize/suggestions/contracts with a version tag ("savings_estimate_v1"). Key fields: estimate_version, scope (route/model/region), recommendation_type (BATCHING|CACHING), baseline_window_start/end, baseline_cost_per_1m_tokens, projected_cost_per_1m_tokens, estimated_monthly_usd_delta, ci_90_low, ci_90_high, confidence_score, and basis_of_estimate (baseline_inputs, assumptions, exclusions). Note: basis_of_estimate is intentionally limited to privacy-safe aggregates (no raw prompts, no request IDs).

Freshness: Baselines are considered valid if updated within the configured freshness SLO (default 6h). If stale, estimator returns STALE_BASELINE with last_updated_at so the service can either suppress the suggestion or show a “may be outdated” banner depending on flag settings.

Testing: Adds unit tests for: (a) estimator math for batching and caching; (b) behavior with partial metering fields; (c) stale baseline gating; (d) monotonicity checks (projected cost should not exceed baseline for positive-savings suggestions unless clamped/invalid); (e) regression coverage for mixed batching + caching suggestions on the same scope to ensure we don’t double-count savings when aggregating in the service.

Rollout/ops: No user-facing behavior in Console is changed directly by this PR, but the payload is now available for suggestions-service to consume. Feature flags and allowlisting remain the responsibility of the Console/BFF layer PRs. Metrics emitted: savings_estimator_v1_success, savings_estimator_v1_invalid_reason (tagged), baseline_freshness_age_hours.

Follow-ups (not in scope): (1) Better calibration of batching throughput multiplier on long-context workloads; (2) Offline validation pipeline + dashboards for estimated vs realized savings; (3) Potential split between “confidence” and “risk” semantics (to be resolved with ADR/UX); (4) Integration to suppress/override estimates when Applied ML guardrails veto a recommendation.

Links: Linear ENG-2403. Related: Suggestions UI/contract integration work in Console PRs, and risk scoring pipeline in a separate PR.
commits: optimize/savings: implement SavingsEstimatorV1 for batching + caching
contracts: introduce savings_estimate_v1 schema + validation helpers
tests: estimator unit tests + stale baseline and missing telemetry cases
metrics: emit estimator outcome + baseline freshness gauges
ci_summary: All checks passing. Unit tests added for estimator math + contract validation. No migrations required; baseline tables already exist (writes to existing aggregate store).
review_conversation: Logan Wright (review): The schema looks good, but can we be explicit about what baseline token volume we’re using for monthly impact? If the window is 7d and we extrapolate to 30d, I want that stated in basis_of_estimate so Console can explain shifts week-to-week.

Nadia Rahman (author): Yep — added basis_of_estimate.monthly_extrapolation: {window_days, scale_factor} and a comment that it’s linear extrapolation. Also added a test that verifies we don’t compute monthly_usd_delta when baseline_token_volume is missing.

Jonas Weber (review): For caching: the hit-rate estimation uses prefix repetition from aggregated stats. Do we have a guardrail if the observed repetition is too low / sample size too small? Otherwise we’ll show noisy savings for low-traffic routes.

Nadia Rahman (author): Added min_sample_tokens and min_requests thresholds; below that we return INVALID_INSUFFICIENT_TELEMETRY with reason details. Confidence_score now incorporates sample size to widen CI bounds as we approach the threshold.

Sana Farid (review): CI math: you’re using a normal approximation around the multiplier. Please clamp CI to [0, +inf) for savings deltas and make sure projected_cost_per_1m_tokens can’t go negative. Also, can we store the variance inputs so we can recalibrate later?

Nadia Rahman (author): Done — projected costs clamped to >= 0, deltas clamped so the lower bound can’t imply negative cost. Added basis_of_estimate.uncertainty_inputs with variance terms (traffic_cv, sample_size, missingness_penalty).

Chloe Martin (review): Please confirm tenant scoping: baseline keys include tenant_id + workspace_id and are not shared across workspaces. Also, we should be careful that basis_of_estimate doesn’t include raw region-level spend that could be sensitive; keep it per-scope only.

Nadia Rahman (author): Confirmed keys include both tenant_id and workspace_id; added an explicit assert in the aggregator call path and a unit test for key construction. basis_of_estimate only includes per-scope aggregates (cost_per_1m + token volume), no cross-scope totals.
Logan Wright (review): One more: we should tag INVALID reasons so we can debug “insufficient telemetry” reports (SUP-19361 type). Can we emit a counter per reason?
Nadia Rahman (author): Added savings_estimator_v1_invalid_reason counter with reason tag (STALE_BASELINE, INSUFFICIENT_TELEMETRY, MISSING_METER_FIELDS, LOW_TRAFFIC).
Jonas Weber (approval): Approved after thresholds + basis fields landed. Let’s track long-context calibration as follow-up.
Logan Wright (approval): Approved. Please ping once this is in staging so we can compare UI output vs metering dashboards.
Chloe Martin (approval): Approved; contract looks stable for Console consumers.
Sana Farid (approval): Approved. Thanks for keeping uncertainty inputs traceable.
